# Maahir Garg

> Maahir Garg is an AI Engineer with AICET's Team Koditsu and a Computer Science and Quantitative Finance student at the National University of Singapore, based in Singapore.

Current facts:

- AICET, Team Koditsu: AI Engineer since Aug 2026. Researching whether behavioural signals from coding-assessment sessions can flag likely cheating. The core result so far is a negative one: a promising 0.778 AUROC model turned out to be statistically indistinguishable from chance, and a lookup of which question a student got scored higher, exposing a confound rather than a detector. He built the detector harness and confound auditor that surfaced this.
- GIC: AI Engineer from Jan to Jul 2026 (former role). Built an internal agentic CLI and sandboxed Chainlit assistant for an 11-person team in a classified-data environment, with custom tools, multi-agent orchestration, step-level guardrails, custom evaluations, and Arize tracing. A Snowflake and SharePoint pipeline automated two manual data sources and reduced evidence retrieval from hours to near-instant.
- NUS teaching: currently teaches CS3230 Design and Analysis of Algorithms and CS3263 Foundations of Artificial Intelligence. Across four teaching semesters, earned a 4.8/5.0 teaching rating against a 4.2 faculty average and a place on the NUS Honour List of Student Tutors.
- Education: Bachelor of Computing (Honours) in Computer Science, Second Major in Quantitative Finance, Minor in Data Engineering, and specialisations in Artificial Intelligence with Distinction, Database Systems, and Computer Networks. GPA 4.71/5.00; expected graduation May 2027.
- Interactive 3D Lab: co-developed an iPhone and Apple Vision Pro tracking framework in collaboration with Apple for stroke-rehabilitation assessment, reaching 89% cross-device accuracy, 30 fps, and sub-millisecond latency. Co-author on a paper in preparation and co-inventor on a patent application in progress (not yet filed).
- PGP Residential Assistant: Residential Assistant at Prince George's Park since May 2025. In September 2026 he sole-built and sole-operated PGPals, the platform for the residence's two-week Emerald Challenge; the event has since closed and the live site is offline.
- Interests: drums, badminton, blitz chess, poker, swimming, Formula 1, and photography.

Selected projects:

- PGPals: full-stack Next.js, TypeScript, and Supabase event platform built and operated alone for a two-week residential challenge. Supported 164 authenticated users across 96 teams, processed 2,297 submissions and 3,763 photo/video attachments across 103 challenges, and closed with zero submissions left pending. The event is over and the site is offline; public source: https://github.com/maahir-garg/pgpals
- Trader's Edge: team final-year project advised by Anand Bhojan, with a working MVP for plain-English strategy specification and historical-data backtesting. The demo requires Google sign-in. Public source is the NUS-FinTechAI team repository.
- Prediction-market engine: read-only research engine over public Polymarket and Kalshi feeds, matching the same real-world question priced differently across venues. It never places a trade, since prediction markets are restricted in Singapore.
- BERT QA compression: reduced a BERT question-answering model 69% in size (440 MB to 128 MB) with no more than 0.5% F1 loss; custom mask-enforced pruning separately reached 54.7% sparsity.
- Domain-specific PEFT: BitFit updated no more than 0.1% of parameters, limited to bias terms, and improved reasoning accuracy from 47% to 73% on clause-extracted health-insurance scenarios.
